findings.state_artifact: tests/e2e/roue-qr-logo-2026-08-13.spec.js -> 01-borne-paysage (and independently reproduced 02-borne-portrait, which never ran in the suite because test.describe.configure({mode:'serial'}) aborts the group after the first failure)
findings.evidence: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/roue-qr-logo-2026-08-13.spec.js --project=chromium --workers=1 --retries=0` FAILS at current HEAD: 'le logo occupe 26.0% du QR, hors de la fourchette sure 15-22%' (assertOverlayLogo, spec line 107, ceiling 0.22). Root cause read directly from source: commit 5253256c2 (2026-08-13 19:19:04, 'logo QR agrandi') bumped borne.blade.php's `.qr-logo` CSS width from 20% to 26% in response to an explicit owner request to make the logo bigger, but (a) never updated the spec's declared safe ceiling (22%) that this exact commit's own predecessor had calibrated, and (b) never updated validation.blade.php's sibling `.qr-logo` (still width:20%, confirmed by direct grep), even though the spec's own comment states the two screens 'posent exactement le meme balisage' -- this is why 03-validation-issue-1/04-validation-issue-2 in the SAME spec run still PASS while 01/02 (borne) FAIL. CRITICALLY: commit 5253256c2 landed at 19:19:04, BEFORE round-2's own confirmed checkpoint HEAD 6adbd819e (19:29:44) and before round-2's report timestamp (19:44:11) -- meaning this regression test was already broken throughout round-2's entire evaluation window, and round-2's regression_sweep (which explicitly listed 5 other specs it re-ran) never re-ran this Wave-A-owned spec, so round-2 declared GREEN without noticing a currently-red committed test. Re-confirmed still red at the round-3 final HEAD (ed9f88d69, which landed two more concurrent-session commits mid-review, neither touching .qr-logo). GROUND TRUTH CHECK (went beyond the failing assertion itself): wrote an independent Playwright probe replicating the exact PIN-login + navigate + screenshot flow, decoded the resulting QR crop with the project's own tests/e2e/helpers/decode-qr.php (same GD decoder the spec uses) for BOTH orientations -- the QR decoded successfully in both landscape (ratio 0.2600) and portrait (ratio 0.2600), returning a well-formed https://www.lecayenne.fr/roue.html?t=... payload each time. So there is no PROVEN real-world scan failure today, but the code's own comment (borne.blade.php, right above .qr-logo) explicitly states 'Toute hausse future se teste avec un vrai telephone, pas a l'oeil' (any future increase must be tested with a real phone, not by eye) -- that real-device validation was never done, and the test's own declared safety margin was silently exceeded and left red.
findings.fix_hint: Either (a) raise the spec's ceiling from 0.22 to something that covers 0.26 AFTER validating real-phone scannability at that coverage (the comment's own bar), and also bump validation.blade.php's .qr-logo to the same 26% for consistency between the two screens that are documented as sharing identical markup, or (b) revert borne.blade.php's .qr-logo width back toward the tested-safe 20-22% range. Either way, this file's CI signal has been silently red since 19:19 today and should be the very next thing fixed before any further vitrine iteration.

findings.state_artifact: account modal heading, ALL states (fresh live capture of the login-connu state: /index.html with lc_known_first/lc_known_last/lc_known_first_at/lecayenne.authPhone seeded exactly as account-retour-connu-2026-08-13.spec.js does; same element/rule also renders 'Bienvenue, chef.' / 'Salut, chef.' on the two other account-v2.jsx states and 'Entre ton code.' on the OTP screen, per shared .lc-acc-title CSS class with no per-state override)
findings.evidence: Visual fresh-eyes pass flagged the heading 'Content de / te revoir,' as looking almost invisible against the white modal, with only the orange 'Julie !' span legible -- verified this was a real bug, not a screenshot-viewing artifact, via direct getComputedStyle(): the h1.lc-acc-title element's OWN text color computes to rgb(251,247,240) (#fbf7f0, the --creme design token), while its rendered background (the nearest ancestor with a non-transparent background-color, div.lc-modal.lc-modal--full) is rgb(255,255,255). Computed WCAG relative-luminance contrast ratio = 1.07:1 (formula per WCAG 2.1, verified by script), against the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text / 3:1 for large bold text. Root cause read in styles.css: `.lc-acc-title` (line 899) has NO color rule at all -- only `.lc-acc-title span { color: var(--orange) }` (line 900) styles the name/keyword span. The plain text nodes therefore inherit color from the DOM ancestor chain, which resolves to `body.lcx-nuit { color: #fbf7f0 }` -- the dark 'night theme' homepage class (added by the 2026-08-08 vitrine V7 redesign) -- because the white `.lc-modal--full` box never resets `color` back to `var(--ink)` for content painted on its own white surface. Confirmed the paragraph text below the heading ('On te reconnait sur cet appareil...') IS legible/dark in the same screenshot, so only this specific un-styled h1 text is affected, not the whole modal. Does not block the primary task path: the email input, the 'Recevoir mon code' button, and the recognition copy remain fully legible and the flow is completable by a sighted user with normal contrast perception; a low-vision user would lose the greeting line specifically. Per REVIEWER_PROTOCOL.md category 4, WCAG contrast defects default to P2 (P1 only if blocking a primary task path, which this is not) -- non-blocking, disclosed only.
findings.fix_hint: Add an explicit `.lc-acc-title { color: var(--ink); }` rule (or scope it under `.lc-modal .lc-acc-title`) so the heading text no longer inherits the dark-theme homepage's cream color when rendered inside the white modal. One-line CSS fix, no JS change needed.
